Cyber Attack Disrupts Bulgarian Payments Network, Commerce Slows Nationwide

Sofia—A widespread cyber attack on Bulgaria’s national payments infrastructure has brought significant disruption to businesses and consumers across the country, with many unable to process electronic transactions as of Thursday afternoon. The incident, which began in the early hours, is ongoing and affecting both in-person and online payments, according to officials.

The National Payments Coordination Centre confirmed that the attack targeted the backbone system facilitating interbank transfers and retail payments. “Our teams are working around the clock to restore service and limit the impact,” said Deputy Minister of Digital Affairs Ivaylo Petrov at a press briefing. “We ask citizens and businesses for patience as we address this unprecedented challenge.”

Retailers in Sofia, Plovdiv, Varna and Burgas reported long queues and growing frustration as card payments were declined at supermarkets, petrol stations, and pharmacies. Many ATMs are also out of service or dispensing limited cash, compounding the problem for people unable to access funds.

“It’s chaos—we can’t pay suppliers, and most customers don’t have enough cash,” said Milena Georgieva, manager of a grocery store in Rousse. “Deliveries are delayed because drivers can’t get fuel. We’re just hoping the system comes back soon.”

The Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce warned that the attack could cause losses running into tens of millions of leva if the disruption drags on. “Small businesses are particularly vulnerable, as they rely heavily on daily electronic transactions,” said Chamber spokesperson Dobromir Kolev.

Mobile payment apps and online banking platforms have also been hit, with users taking to social media to voice concerns and seek updates. The Union of Bulgarian Employers called for greater investment in cyber security, saying the incident “shows just how dependent the economy has become on digital infrastructure.”

Authorities have not disclosed who may be behind the attack or provided a precise timeline for restoration of the payments system. The Ministry of Interior said law enforcement and cyber defense agencies are investigating, and regional police have increased patrols around bank branches.

As the situation unfolds, officials urge Bulgarians to limit non-essential travel and purchases, and to use cash where possible. Further updates are expected as efforts to restore the payments network continue.
